## Description

A narrow column along the right of the list, always shown, whether or not the list has anything to scroll. It is the list's only scrollbar: no scrollbar is laid over the list, or appears only while hovering or scrolling.

## Surface

Every scrollbar is this one, wherever it is. It has no background of its own: the column takes the colour of the surface it sits on, so on the file tree it is the tree's colour, and on a panel's body the body's. Nothing in it is a colour of its own; its border, buttons, thumb, the thumb's ends, the arrows, and the lightening of the thumb and buttons are all white or black laid over that surface, so the scrollbar looks the same on any of them.
The strengths given here are dark mode's. Light mode takes the same steps, its raised parts lighter than the surface as in dark mode: the border, buttons, and thumb are white laid about a third of the way over the surface, the thumb's ends about a sixth, and the thumb and buttons lighten with white laid a fifth of the way while hovered and two fifths while pressed or dragged. Its arrows are darker than the buttons rather than lighter, black laid about a third of the way over them, since white would all but vanish on a light surface.

## Buttons

A square button at the top of the column scrolls the list up a little, and a square button at the bottom scrolls it down a little. The column is 18 pixels wide, and each button is 17 pixels tall, as wide as the column. A button is raised over the surface just as the thumb is, #222222 on #111111 in dark mode, with no bevel, border, or line of its own. It shows a small solid arrow, pointing up or down, 6 pixels wide and 4 tall, centred across it, 7 pixels from its top pointing up and from its bottom pointing down, drawn crisp on whole pixels rather than smoothed, in a faint grey, #4d4d4d on the 

## Track

Between the buttons runs the track, from just beneath the top button to just above the bottom one. The track has no fill: it is the surface it sits on, #111111 on the file tree in dark mode. The whole column is bordered by a line a pixel wide down both its sides, in the buttons' and thumb's colour, #222222 in dark mode, so the border runs straight into the buttons at the top and bottom and the column reads as one raised outline around the track. No line runs across the column, and nothing in it is drawn in the theme's border colour.
The track holds a thumb as tall as the share of the list in view, and never too short to grab, placed as far down the track as the list is scrolled. The thumb is a plain rectangle, as wide as the column, the border and all, with no rounded corners and no bevel, raised over the surface, #222222 on #111111 in dark mode, white laid about 7% of the way over it, so it is brighter than the track. Its top and bottom ends each have a single row of pixels, between the borders, half way between the track and the thumb, #191919 in dark mode, softening where the track meets it. It lightens a step while th
Pressing the thumb and dragging scrolls the list with it for as long as the button is held, even once the pointer leaves the column, and pressing the track elsewhere moves the thumb there, from where it can be dragged straight away. Where a resize edge beside the list overlaps the column, a press goes to whichever of the two has the smaller hit area, as the main window says.

## Steadiness

The thumb never jumps. Its size and place always reflect the whole list's real height, including a list that only draws the rows in view: every row is measured, even those never scrolled into view, so the thumb doesn't grow, shrink, or leap as rows come into view. A row that arrives, or changes, while out of view counts at its height as soon as it does, and after the list's width changes, rewrapping its rows, the height is known in full again by the next frame. Only what has changed is measured again, so a long list stays as quick to scroll and to add to as one that measures only what is in vi
A row's height is the same measured out of view as drawn in it. Text in a row, such as a reply's markdown, is parsed once and kept for as long as the app runs, not only while its row is drawn, so a row scrolled away and back is never parsed again, nor shorter for a moment while it is. Long text is parsed in the background, so a row holding it may first measure short: while it parses, its row is measured again every fraction of a second, for a few seconds at most, so the height is right as soon as the parse lands, whether or not the row is in view. Dragging the thumb, it stays under the pointer

The Tasks list in the right sidebar now uses the standard pinned scrollbar. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 84 files.

- **Always shown:** an 18px column along the tab's right edge, there even when nothing needs scrolling.
- **Full height:** it runs the whole height of the tab, beside the pinned headings as well as the rows.
- **Fixed in place:** it never scrolls with the list, never appears only on hover, and is never laid over the rows.
- **Alignment:** headings, day dividers and rows all stop at its left edge, so times and heading controls line up against it.
- **Thumb:** sized from the whole list, leaving out rows hidden under pinned headings and collapsed sections. Scrolling to the bottom shows the last row whole.
- **No bottom lock:** the list isn't continuously growing output, so it has no lock-to-bottom button.

"Pinned scrollbar situation" could mean something else; I read it as the app's always-shown scrollbar column. If you meant something different, tell me.
